item.title: Cape Sata: Japan's Southern Tip — Guide
item.description: Cape Sata (Sata-misaki), at the tip of the Osumi Peninsula, is the southernmost point of mainland Japan (Kyushu), a wild and scenic headland marking the very edge of the country’s main islands. Reached by a scenic drive down the peninsula and a walk through lush subtropical vegetation, the cape offers dramatic coastal scenery: rugged cliffs plunging into the deep blue sea, sweeping views across the water, and on clear days sightings of distant islands including Yakushima and Tanegashima on the horizon.

item.title: Cape Zanpa — Guide
item.description: Cape Zanpa (Zanpa-misaki), on the west coast of Okinawa’s main island in Yomitan Village, is a striking headland where rugged coral limestone cliffs drop about 30 metres to the crashing sea. At its tip stands a tall white lighthouse — one of the few in Okinawa you can climb — offering panoramic views over the East China Sea and the wild, wave-battered coastline from the top. The cape’s raw, windswept scenery, with its jagged rocks, blowholes and open horizon, is a dramatic contrast to Okinawa’s calm beaches, and it’s a renowned spot for watching the sun sink into the ocean.

item.title: Irago Cape and the Atsumi Peninsula: Lighthouse at Land's End — Guide
item.description: Irago Cape marks the tip of the Atsumi Peninsula, the long green arm that encloses Mikawa Bay, and its white lighthouse — one of Japan’s fifty famous lighthouses — stands on the rocks where the bay’s calm waters meet the open Pacific swell. Beside it curves Koijigahama, the ‘Beach of the Road of Love’, a kilometre of pale sand celebrated in poetry and popular with couples, while the peninsula behind is one of Japan’s most productive flower and vegetable coasts, blanketed in yellow rapeseed blossom each early spring and serving some of Aichi’s best seafood in the port shacks around the ferry terminal.

item.title: Echizen Misaki Lighthouse: A Dramatic Cliffside Coastal Lighthouse — Guide
item.description: Echizen Misaki Lighthouse sits perched on rugged cliffs at the tip of the Echizen Peninsula, offering magnificent views of the open Sea of Japan and access to atmospheric coastal walking trails winding along the promontory. The austere beauty of this remote headland, considerably less visited than Fukui’s more famous Tojinbo Cliffs, makes it a good choice for travellers seeking solitude and dramatic seascape photography away from larger crowds. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Echizen, Fukui Hours Always accessible (exterior); lighthouse grounds daylight hours Admission Free Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Choshi Guide: Cape Inubo, Soy Sauce & Seafood Access
item.description: At the far northeastern tip of Chiba, the port city of Choshi is where the Tone River meets the Pacific — a place famous for three things: soy sauce, seafood and sunrises. Pounded by the open ocean, Cape Inubosaki is one of the first places in mainland Japan to see the New Year’s sunrise, marked by a handsome white lighthouse you can climb. Choshi is also one of Japan’s great soy sauce towns (home to Yamasa and Higeta), where you can tour breweries and taste the difference, and one of its busiest fishing ports, serving superb sashimi and grilled fish.
